## Motivation

Most analytics work starts from a blank page, which means most analytics work starts with re-deriving the same scaffolding: What should a measurement plan contain? What belongs in a dashboard? What checks should every pipeline have before anyone trusts it?

The blank page is where good projects go to die — or worse, where inconsistent ones survive. When every project invents its own structure, the organization pays a tax on every handoff, review, and rehire.

## Scope

A small set of templates, each with an example, a checklist, and a short "why" — opinionated enough to be useful, small enough to actually get adopted:

- **Measurement plan** — decisions, definitions, grain, windows, owners.
- **Metrics definition doc** — the one-pager that stops "revenue means six things."
- **Dashboard scaffold** — hero metric, two supporting metrics, nothing decorative.
- **Experiment plan** — hypothesis, power analysis, guardrails, stopping rules.
- **Pipeline hygiene checklist** — freshness, volume, schema, null-rate checks.

## Status & roadmap

- [ ] Measurement plan template (first)

## What success looks like

A team other than mine uses one of the templates without me in the room — and the resulting document is good enough that I'd have signed off on it.
